surveys.summary: Identity/authz in oyatie is a strong pure-domain library layer with almost no I/O-bearing runtime. The bespoke human IdP (oya/identity/crates/oya-identity, ADR-0476) is a 156-line empty shell, but workload identity is a real, well-tested library PEP (axum REST + tonic gRPC, real ES256/EdDSA JWT validation, real cedar-policy 4.11 evaluation) that lacks a binary and durable storage. Real Cedar evaluation runs today inside exactly two runnable binaries (cloud-intelligence-app, ci-webhook-gateway-app); the dedicated oya/policy "Cedar" service is a hand-rolled Cedar-shaped evaluator with NO cedar-policy dependency, and the ADR-0243 universal gate is explicitly unimplemented per its own spec. Tenancy, KMS, and secrets are pure models/request-shape adapters with no DB or network clients; dogfood-grade IdP+PDP needs a serving binary, persistence, and a real central PDP, but the kernels to build them on are genuinely substantial (~16.4k lines in identity crates alone).

CODE REALITY: the fastest credible path to a REAL running product is the workload-identity PEP + a real central Cedar PDP + tenant-rbac, because (a) oya/identity/crates/oya-identity-workload-rest already has a real axum build_router (verified line 385) with fail-closed PEP semantics + real aws-lc-rs ES256/EdDSA JWT validation, missing only a [[bin]] + durable store; (b) Cedar already runs in 2 real binaries (cloud-intelligence-app verified has main.rs, ci-webhook-gateway-app) using cedar-policy 4.11 (verified 5 crates) — the embedded-PDP pattern is proven and copyable; (c) oya/tenant-rbac has 33k LOC of tenancy contracts to back the packaging axis. infra_gap_list: [1 — FOUNDATION, no deps] Durable persistence substrate. CURRENT: zero sqlx/postgres dependency anywhere in identity/policy/tenancy/IAM/KMS; oya-tenant-rbac-postgres-rls-storage deliberately opens no DB (verified lib.rs:5-8); all stores in-memory. NEEDED: a real Postgres adapter with tenant RLS (app.tenant_id GUC), wired behind the existing storage ports. This unblocks every stateful service.

[2 — depends on persistence] Central Cedar PDP (policy engine). CURRENT: cedar-policy 4.11 runs embedded in 2 binaries (cloud-intelligence-app, ci-webhook-gateway-app) but there is NO standalone PDP; oya/policy/oya-policy-cedar-* is a hand-rolled evaluator with no cedar-policy dep; ADR-0243 universal gate is unimplemented by its own admission (specs/cloud-authorization-target.json non_claims). NEEDED: a runnable PDP binary wrapping real cedar-policy, default-deny, loading identity.cedar + per-tenant policy fragments, exposed as a /authorize service the PEPs call. Copy the proven cloud-intelligence CedarAuthzGate pattern.

[3 — depends on persistence + PDP] Human IdP serving binary. CURRENT: oya-identity binary is a 156-line TODO stub (verified main.rs: 'TODO(ADR-0476): wire subsystems'); workload-identity has a real axum build_router (verified line 385) + real ES256/EdDSA JWT (aws-lc-rs) but no [[bin]] and in-memory store; oya-identity-oidc-issuer-kernel (2k LOC) models RFC8414/9068 but has no HTTP server or signer impl. NEEDED: wrap workload-rest in a [[bin]], wire the durable principal store, mount the OIDC issuer kernel behind a JWS signer (aws-lc-rs), load identity.cedar via the PDP. Workload IdP reaches dogfood in ~1 focused sprint; human-login/sessions/WebAuthn/refresh is the longer tail.

[4 — depends on persistence] KMS/secrets live backend. CURRENT: cloud-kms adapters (openbao/oci) are pure command-shape translators with NO HTTP client (verified); cloud-secrets is file-adapter dev-grade only. NEEDED: a live OpenBao Transit client behind the existing KmsProviderCryptoPort (cloud-intelligence already has oya-cloud-intelligence-openbao-adapter as a reference) so JWT signing keys + tenant encryption keys are real.

[5 — depends on services existing] Observability collector + SLO authoring. CURRENT: cloud-observability is 3 library crates, no binary, no slos/ dir; CLAUDE.md path cloud/observability/ is wrong. NEEDED: a runnable collector binary AND {oya,cloud}/<service>/slos/*.openslo.yaml for every FD-001 surface before promotion (enforced by the live oya-cloud-ci-slo-coverage-app gate). This is a hard ADR-0130 promotion gate.

[6 — depends on all above] One-command/one-click Kubernetes deployment. CURRENT: cloud-iac has a runnable CLI (oya-cloud-iac-app) but no service ships reproducible k8s setup evidence; FD-001 exit demands 11 host targets + 22 artifacts (OpenTofu/IaC, GitOps, multi-arch OCI, SBOM/provenance, distroless images, Talos join, restore evidence). NEEDED: per-surface OpenTofu modules + GitOps + distroless OCI build, gated by conformance. This is the FD-001 exit bar, built last per surface.

[7 — cross-cutting, build incrementally] Tenant lifecycle + isolation control plane. CURRENT: cloud/tenancy has 14 crates but 12 are <70-line micro-stubs; specs/tenant-model.json is Proposed/advisory; cloud/cloud-tenancy duplicates as a thin CLI. NEEDED: real tenant create/suspend/retire + isolation-posture enforcement backing the FD-001 'core' packaging axis, consolidated to one canonical tenancy dir.

goal_stories.acceptance: (a) oya-application-shell-frontend-prototype is promoted from mock-only: src/server_mock_catalog.rs replaced by live fetches from the Story-3/4 backends; the crate builds with ssr+hydrate features in the workspace and app-shell-codegen (pnpm codegen:check) lane stays green. (b) tenant-context-switcher, ops-deployment-status-panel, audit-evidence-timeline, and policy-disclosure-banner are implemented per their specs/design-system/*.json contracts (test_refs pass); the context switcher has a test proving no cached state leaks across personal/work/admin-audit pillars. (c) libs/oya-check-client-stack-discipline extended with the ADR-0393 superseded-reference lint so SolidJS/SolidStart imports fail the check (unit test asserts rejection); the archived oya/app-shell-frontend TS app is untouched. PR oya-ci-required green, signed, no generated.json.
depends_on: Tenancy+RBAC Core Vertical to Production Depth

goal_stories.title: Dogfooding Wiring
goal_stories.objective: Wire the platform to dogfood itself — the IdP authenticates the shell, Cedar gates real operator actions, observability ingests the platform's own telemetry — so the product runs the product.
goal_stories.acceptance: (a) The Leptos shell authenticates real operators via the Story-3 IdP (OIDC login round-trip succeeds in an E2E). (b) Operator actions in the shell (tenant create/suspend) are authorized by the central Cedar PDP and produce audit records visible in the audit-evidence-timeline component. (c) The observability collector ingests the IdP+PDP+tenancy services' own metrics and a dashboard renders their SLO/error-budget state. (d) A documented one-command bring-up (OpenTofu apply + GitOps sync) stands the whole slice up on local Kubernetes and the dogfood smoke test passes. Mechanically checkable: E2E test names + smoke-test exit 0. PR oya-ci-required green, signed, no generated.json.
depends_on: Unified Leptos Shell Hosting the Module

goal_stories.title: Pipeline-as-Product Ratchet
goal_stories.objective: Convert every friction/failure encountered during delivery into an enforced gate or automation, per the pipeline-as-product doctrine (ADR-0519/0528/0529), closing the verified gate-registration blind spot first.
goal_stories.acceptance: (a) The branch-local oya-cloud-ci-rust-first-automation-hygiene-app (verified BUCK-only, no Cargo.toml, escapes gate_registration) is either registered (Cargo.toml + oya-ci-required.yml matrix + oya-ci.toml gates.enabled) OR the gate_registration meta-test in oya-cloud-ci-firewall-app/tests/gate_registration.rs is extended to enumerate gates by directory presence and fail-closed on any Buck-only gate not in the matrix (unit test proves a Buck-only gate now fails registration). (b) The planning-closure gate logic is migrated out of the retirement-candidate oya-dev-cli into a cloud-ci gate crate. (c) The ADR-0528 oya-ci-gate-contract crate is created (centralizing the per-gate-duplicated Finding/evaluate_keyed) with at least one gate carrying a remediation tier in gate-disposition.json (ADR-0519/0529 AUTO/ADVISE/GATE field present, meta-gate rejects untagged codes). (d) At least two concrete frictions hit during Stories 2-6 (e.g. a missing slos file, an in-memory store regression) are encoded as new fail-closed gates with labeled-fixture tests. Mechanically checkable: new gate tests pass + every gate dir appears in the matrix (the invariant is now enforceable). PR oya-ci-required green, signed, no generated.json.

goal_stories.title: Final Quality Gate
goal_stories.objective: Run a separate-lane quality pass — AI-slop cleanup, independent verification, and code review — so the slice exits at honest industry-leading depth with no false green.
goal_stories.acceptance: (a) ai-slop-cleaner pass over the slice removes dead scaffolding/comments and any remaining mock paths (diff reviewed). (b) An independent verifier (not the authoring context) confirms the dogfood E2E + smoke test + all cloud-ci gates green on a clean checkout, with evidence captured under evidence/. (c) code-reviewer APPROVE is recorded on the final PR; no crate in the slice contains 'TODO(ADR'/stub-main patterns (grep=0); no *.generated.json in any diff; all commits SSH-signed; oya-ci-required green and the reviewer-APPROVE + green-context completion gate satisfied before merge to dev. Mechanically checkable: grep counts, gate status, reviewer disposition, signature verification.

risks: Scope-vs-depth trap: FD-001 mandates 11 surfaces at full production depth (not MVP) with a ~79-rule architecture exit bar + 11 host targets + 22 artifacts + KR localization. The 8 stories deliver the tenancy/RBAC CORE slice end-to-end as the proof point; the remaining 10 surfaces (messenger/mail/community/workflow/ontology/intelligence/canonical-base/KR-pack) and full host-target matrix are deliberately NOT covered and must serialize after. Treating this plan as 'all of FD-001' would itself be a false-green.

Persistence is the critical-path bottleneck: nothing in identity/policy/tenancy/IAM/KMS touches a real database today (verified: zero sqlx/postgres deps). Story 2 must land a real Postgres-RLS adapter or Stories 3-6 cannot become stateful running services; underestimating this single gap risks cascading slip.

Human-login IdP is months out: only workload-identity is ~1 sprint from dogfood. Full human IdP (sessions, WebAuthn ceremonies end-to-end, refresh tokens, client registration) per ADR-0476 has only kernel shapes (oidc-issuer-kernel, webauthn-server-kernel) with zero I/O. The dogfood story should authenticate operators via the workload/OIDC path; do not promise full consumer-grade human login in this slice.

Cedar PDP centralization risk: the embedded pattern works in 2 binaries, but extracting a central PDP that every PEP calls adds a network hop and a single-point-of-failure; the hand-rolled oya-policy-cedar-* evaluator must be retired/re-scoped carefully so two decision algorithms never coexist (current repo has exactly that contradiction).

Pipeline-as-product feedback loop can stall delivery: if every friction must become a gate before proceeding, Story 7 could balloon. Bound it — encode the verified blind spot (Buck-only gate-registration) + a small fixed number of real frictions, not an open-ended audit.

SSOT-store DRAFT status: all three registry/stores/*.json self-describe as DRAFT pending founder door:one-way sign-off; planning that treats them as ratified canon may be reversed at sign-off. Authority for this plan rests on HANDOFF + masterplan planning_authority + ADRs, not the draft stores.

Frontend stack drift: ADR-0393 promised a superseded-reference lint that does not exist, and per-product web clients may still legally be SvelteKit (oya/workflow-studio/clients/web-sveltekit) while the app-shell must be Leptos. Without the lint (Story 5), SolidJS/React could silently reappear; the discipline check does not yet encode ADR-0393 supersession.

Generated-faces discipline: HANDOFF guardrail 8 + the generated-output-diff-policy CI job forbid committing add/modify *.generated.json. The session-start 3 dirty files were already resolved (git status verified clean), but every PR in this plan must regenerate-not-commit these faces or the diff-policy lane fails closed.

Signing enforcement gap: live GitHub API shows required_signatures.enabled=false on dev (branch-protection.yaml is a self-described shadow record), while guardrails mandate SSH-signing. Signed commits are convention/target here, not live-enforced — acceptance criteria assume signing but cannot rely on GitHub to reject unsigned commits until the ruleset is actually applied.
